newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Councils confirm Lyttelton share sales.
newsitem.headline: Councils confirm Lyttelton share sales.

text.p: Two local councils from South Island confirmed on Thursday they had sold the bulk of their shares in Lyttelton Port Company to AMP in a single trade of about 7.8 million shares at NZ$1.90 per share earlier today.

Banks Peninsula District Council chief executive Mike Jones told Reuters the sale of just over 3.88 million shares at $1.90 had represented about 3.9 percent of Lyttelton's total shares in issue. He said the sale would improve cashflow income and allow an extra $350,000 of extra income for the council each year.
"We were wanting to release the immense capital gain that has been realised over the last 10 months (since float)," he said. The shares were floated last July at $1.00.
Banks Peninsula had retained some 80,000 shares, he added.
Brian Lester, finance and trading manager of Waimakariri District Council, the other partner in the joint venture which sold its shares, said his council had not retained any.
He confirmed that AMP was the buyer, as market sources had told Reuters earlier.
"We received an offer and looked at that and compared it with the return. We can reinvest those funds and get $350,000 a year, about 3 percent of our rates," Lester added.
